draft.title: Votes for women and early reforms
card: In 1894 South Australia gave women the vote in colonial elections. It was also the first colony to let women stand for parliament.
In 1902 the new federal parliament gave women the right to vote and to stand in federal elections. Australia was among the first countries to do this.
Most First Nations people were shut out. The 1902 law excluded Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people unless they were already on a state roll, and in practice most could not vote.

Early reforms followed. An aged pension (1908) gave money to older people who could not support themselves. The basic wage (1907 Harvester judgment) set a minimum pay meant to support a worker's family.
draft.remember: Women won the vote in 1894 and 1902, but First Nations people were mostly left out.

a.q: Which statement about the federal vote in 1902 is correct?
opts: Women won it, but most First Nations people were shut out
Women won it, and all First Nations people could also vote
Only women in South Australia won the federal vote
Men and women won the federal vote together that year
a.why: The 1902 law gave non-Indigenous women the federal vote, but it excluded most Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. The tempting option saying everyone could vote is wrong because the exclusion was part of the law.
a.clue: Think about who was left out of the new law.

b.q: Which early reform was meant to give older people who could not support themselves some income?
opts: The aged pension
The basic wage
The dictation test
The vote for women
b.why: The aged pension paid money to older people who could not support themselves. The basic wage is the tempting wrong answer: it was a minimum pay for workers, not a payment to older people.
b.clue: Which reform was for people no longer working?

a.best: Women won it, but most First Nations people were shut out

problems.detail: "Women won the vote in 1894 and 1902" could suggest all Australian women won the vote in 1894. The card says only South Australian women did, in colonial elections. Say "South Australian women won the vote in 1894".
